decision: ACCEPT Peerit release sequence 22 as the LIVE bounded-public-test launch successor: a compression-tolerant bounded runtime asset fetch (verify the DECOMPRESSED payload against the signed length and hash bounds when a response carries content-encoding, while keeping the strict uncompressed path byte-for-byte when it does not), keeping the limited Cell-GET runtime authority EXPOSED at sequence 22 and signed seed recovery ENABLED for the same 34-record live launch seed. The exact production CSP remains unchanged, authenticated browser authority MUST become active before any relay I/O, recovery performs zero network PUTs, ordinary delivery remains LOCAL_ONLY, the all-five successor remains excluded, and the GA product gate remains blocked with all 22 blockers disclosed-open.

authority.owner_instruction: Second host-compat unblock on the live site. The seq-21 content-type fix WORKED (live DOM probe: pinHistory state=verified-production-pin-history, active=true). The boot then failed at the next check: authority state=blocked-authenticated-browser-runtime with releaseBlockers=["BROWSER_RUNTIME_ASSET_LENGTH_INVALID"], message "/icon.svg Content-Length exceeds or differs from its signed bound". MECHANISM (confirmed against the live host): Render's Cloudflare-backed edge compresses text assets (Brotli/gzip) when the client sends accept-encoding (browsers always do); the header Content-Length then carries the COMPRESSED size (or is absent), while browser-runtime-authority.mjs required the header to equal the signed UNCOMPRESSED bound exactly. The compressed length differs -> BROWSER_RUNTIME_ASSET_LENGTH_INVALID -> authority blocked -> seed recovery blocked -> empty site. The asset manifest pins bytes by hash, not by compressed length, so the strict model is preserved by verifying the decompressed payload against the signed length and hash bounds. Patch compression-tolerant without weakening anything; release as sequence 22.

compression_fix.root_cause: Render's Cloudflare-backed edge compresses text assets (Brotli/gzip) whenever the client sends accept-encoding; the Content-Length header then carries the COMPRESSED size or is absent, while browser-runtime-authority.mjs required it to equal the signed UNCOMPRESSED bound exactly -> BROWSER_RUNTIME_ASSET_LENGTH_INVALID on the first text asset (/icon.svg).
compression_fix.acceptance_rule: when a response carries content-encoding (br/gzip/any non-identity token), the Content-Length header may be the compressed size or absent and is not compared to the signed bound; the DECOMPRESSED payload's byte length must equal the signed length bound exactly (runtime asset fetcher) and the signed hash bindings apply unchanged (blake2b256 per asset in the canonical WebAssetManifestV1 for the runtime assets; the signed JSON file-hash comparisons in release coherence); when there is no content-encoding, the existing strict behavior (exact integer Content-Length equal to the signed bound) is preserved byte-for-byte on BOTH fetchers; HTML/error responses stay rejected; deadlines and fail-closed codes unchanged
compression_fix.unit_coverage: test/peerit-binary-content-types.mjs compression matrix: br/gzip with compressed or absent Content-Length + exact decompressed bytes PASS; shorter-than-bound decompressed payload FAILS (BROWSER_RUNTIME_ASSET_LENGTH_INVALID); same-length tampered decompressed payload FAILS the signed hash binding; uncompressed response with drifted Content-Length FAILS (strict path preserved); compressed HTML FAILS (BROWSER_RUNTIME_ASSET_CONTENT_TYPE_INVALID)
